text:
maria: Heads-up — prod token/sec (eu-west-1) dropped ~18% after the last canary. Continuous batcher queueing spike: median queue time 15ms -> 120ms
maria: Dashboard: https://dash.company/redwood/ctb/eu-west-1 (captures token/sec, queue_time, kv_hitrate)
kenji: saw it. attach profiler: when queueing spikes, kernel fallback to kernel_x_memcpy increases CPU memcpy%. suspect kernel-selection path choosing memcpy-friendly kernel for small batches
kenji: perf snippet:
```
perf top -p <pid> --sort comm
# kernel_x_memcpy  42%  (memcpy)
# kernel_y_opt     3%   (matmul)
```
sasha: bisect landed on commit f9c3b7d (scheduler: change prefetch window & age-weighting). rolling back the window change in my local bisect reduces queueing in repro
deploy-bot: Canary deployment 2026-03-16T21:14:03 started for service:inference(rollout-id=rl-77)
tara: kv cache hitrate down ~7% across tokens. warmup takes longer after the scheduling change — more small batches means less shared prefixes
tara: suggestion: revert prefetch-window change behind feature flag or reduce age-weight influence
jordan: pushed revert branch: revert/scheduler/prefetch-window-f9c3b7d, canarying on cluster-a now. logs:
```
[info] canary cluster-a: token/sec baseline restored within ~5m
[warn] kv: warmup lag improved but still 2% below long-term
```
maria: thanks. can we add CI perf gate: median queue_time(99pct) < 50ms for 10k synthetic requests? also gate on kv_hitrate >= 95% for warmup scenario
kenji: adding a perf test and a kernel-selection assertion — ensure no fallback to kernel_x_memcpy for batch sizes > 4
sasha: adding a deployment metric for kv/hitrate + queue p99, will alert on 5% regression
jordan: canary shows token/sec back to baseline, holding rollout until revert merges and CI perf gates pass :thumbsup:
maria: great, assign follow-ups in the rollback PR and postmortem notes. thanks everyone :heart:
